pathway.title: Weatherford International plc — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The first finding a committee must read is that Weatherford carries little leverage on every measure the sources allow. Total debt of USD 1,480 million is 1.48x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,001 million and 1.71x EBITDA before add-backs of USD 867 million; net debt of USD 282 million is 0.28x. The ratio on the company's definition has crept up from 1.39x at 2025-12-31 because trailing EBITDA fell while debt was flat, and net leverage fell only because cash rose. [CP-1 leverage chart data and calculations 5 and 6]. The mechanism is that low leverage gives room to absorb a further earnings decline, but the cushion is in cash that is partly trapped, not in falling debt.

The second finding is that liquidity is strong and the near-term maturity is already funded. Cash of USD 1,161 million is 4.40x the current portion of long-term debt of USD 264 million, which is mostly the 2030 notes that Weatherford called on 2026-10-20 for redemption from cash on 2026-10-30. Undrawn commitments are USD 766 million after letters of credit, of which only about USD 599 million can be borrowed for cash on the facility split disclosed in the annual report. Liquidity is 1.30x total debt, or 1.19x on the cash-drawable basis. Redemption completion is not evidenced, and the pro forma net debt after it would be about the same, since the notes are repaid with cash. [CP-1 liquidity, calculations 8 and 11; CP-1A transaction summary]

The third finding is that earnings are weakening in 2026 and cash flow quality is lower than it looks. Nine-month 2026 revenue of USD 3,400 million is 6.3% below USD 3,629 million a year earlier and operating income of USD 383 million is 31.2% below USD 557 million, because the Iran Conflict cut Middle East, North Africa and Asia revenue even though oil prices and rig counts were higher. Operating cash flow rose to USD 503 million from USD 408 million only through a working capital release of USD 65 million against an outflow of USD 116 million, so cash flow before working capital fell by USD 86 million. The mechanism is operating leverage on a fixed cost base plus receivable timing, and it matters because free cash flow supports both debt service and shareholder payouts. [CP-1 cash flow tables and calculation 10; CP-1A operating model rows on the Iran Conflict and cost structure]

The fourth finding is that concentrated receivables, trapped cash and contingent instruments can reduce usable liquidity. The largest Mexican customer was 14% of net receivables at 2026-09-30 and has a history of late payment; about USD 164 million of cash cannot be immediately repatriated, with USD 128 million held in Russian operations; and letters of credit and surety bonds totalling USD 1,065 million sit outside debt and can be called on breach of contract or performance. That total is 0.72x total debt and is not additive to the liquidity measure. [CP-1 claims outside the debt total; CP-1A concentration rows]

The fifth finding is that the capital structure and legal perimeter are in transition and the sources do not describe the lender effects. Debt was refinanced into 6.75% notes due 2033 in 2025, NCS Multistage was acquired mostly for shares, and entities were added as co-issuers of the notes, most recently on 2026-09-25. The parent has shareholder approval to move from Ireland to a Delaware corporation, subject to court sanction, with a planned intellectual property transition under evaluation. The mechanism is that obligor, guarantor and collateral arrangements could change while the documents that govern them are not available. [CP-1A transaction summary, governance table and conflicts table]

runs.text: Strengths. Low reported leverage (Documentary Fact): total debt is 1.48x and net debt 0.28x of trailing company-defined adjusted EBITDA, and the interest burden is light, with adjusted EBITDA 9.02x trailing cash interest paid [CP-1]. Large liquidity (Documentary Fact): USD 1,161 million of cash and USD 766 million of undrawn commitments, with zero borrowings on the facility [CP-1]. A refinanced, longer debt profile (Documentary Fact): most bond debt now matures in 2033 and the remaining 2030 notes are called, which the company expects to reduce annualized cash interest by about USD 20 million (Management Language) [CP-1; CP-1A timeline]. Diversified operations (Documentary Fact): three well-lifecycle segments across about 75 countries, with most revenue earned internationally [CP-1A operating model]. Free cash flow covers payouts (Analyst Interpretation): nine-month 2026 adjusted free cash flow of USD 379 million exceeded the shareholder return of USD 113 million, which is 29.8% of it, and no debt-funded distribution is evidenced [CP-1; CP-1A ownership and capital allocation]. No sponsor or extraction behaviour is documented (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A governance table].

Weaknesses. Earnings are cyclical and falling in 2026 (Documentary Fact): revenue and operating income are lower and adjusted EBITDA for nine months fell 8.5% to USD 710 million from USD 776 million [CP-1]. Cash flow before working capital fell (Analyst Interpretation): the rise in reported operating cash flow depends on receivable collections that may not repeat [CP-1]. Regional and customer concentration (Documentary Fact): the largest region is the disrupted one, a Mexican customer has a late payment history, and Russia carries sanctions and cash access risk [CP-1A]. Fixed cost leverage (Documentary Fact): cost of products and services rose to 69% of revenue from 65% in FY2025 as costs fell more slowly than revenue [CP-1A]. Definition and covenant opacity (Insufficient Information): adjusted EBITDA is company-defined and covenant ratios and definitions are not reported, so headroom cannot be measured [CP-1]. Structural transition (Insufficient Information): the effect of the redomestication and the intellectual property transition on guarantors and collateral is undescribed, and ownership beyond a widely held listing is undisclosed [CP-1A].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: New debt issues: the sources show one new bond issue in the last two years and none in 2026. On 2025-10-06 Weatherford International Ltd. issued 6.75% senior notes due 2033-10-15 (principal 1.2 billion as printed); the tender offer and redemption of most of the 8.625% senior notes due 2030 used the proceeds of that issue and cash on hand, and the company recorded a 39 loss on extinguishment and redemption premium (10-K page:84 and page:44; Documentary Fact). The mechanism for a creditor is lower coupon and a maturity pushed from 2030 to 2033 on most of the bond debt, with the stub of the 2030 notes (principal about 236) left outstanding until the October 2026 call. On 2025-09-18 the credit agreement was amended to raise the commitment from 720 to 1 billion with an accordion to 1.15 billion and to extend its maturity (10-K page:55; Documentary Fact); the amendment text is not supplied. No new borrowing is reported in the nine months to 2026-09-30 (CP-1 cash flow table; Q3 10-Q page:3 and page:4).

Acquisition: on 2026-05-31 Weatherford signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire NCS Multistage Holdings, Inc. for shares or a mix of shares and cash, subject to proration (Q2 10-Q page:14), and it closed on 2026-09-01 for total consideration of 128, made up of 13 cash net of cash acquired, 1.0 million ordinary shares valued at 101 and 7 for assumed equity awards (Q3 10-Q page:15; Documentary Fact). The acquired business brought tangible assets of 150, intangible assets and goodwill of 46 and liabilities of 34, plus 34 of noncontrolling interest (page:15). Management states that it expects "at least $15 million of cost synergies upon closing and integration" (Q2 release page:2; Management Language, not adopted). Mechanism: because most consideration was shares and assumed awards, the deal added little cash outflow or debt, so leverage effects are limited, but the 10-Q does not say whether NCS carried debt, and integration risk and cost remain. Appetite for further acquisitions is not inferred from one deal. The Q3 10-Q records that Advent-NCS Acquisition Limited Partnership, NCS's largest shareholder, received 357,159 shares, resold under a registered prospectus supplement (page:38); this is not a control position.

Redomestication: the first proposal (Ireland to Texas, announced 2026-04-02) received over 60% support but not the 75% needed and failed in June 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:12; Q2 release page:5). An updated proposal to redomesticate to Delaware was approved by shareholders on 2026-09-03 and is subject to sanction by the High Court of Ireland and other steps, with completion expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:16). Management expects annual cash savings of 20 to 30 from 2027 (Q3 release page:6; Management Language). Related restructuring activities, including the planned intellectual property transition, are "being evaluated for their potential accounting and tax implications" (Q3 10-Q page:16). Creditor mechanism: a change of parent and a transfer of intellectual property can alter which entities hold assets, who guarantees the debt and how the collateral is arranged, and whether credit agreement or indenture conditions apply. The sources do not describe any of those effects, so the lender impact is Insufficient Information and the pending status must be carried into every consumer. The 2026-09-25 supplemental indenture adding Weatherford International Holding LLC as co-issuer of the 2033 notes and releasing its guarantee (Q3 10-Q page:10 and page:39) may be a step in this reorganisation, but the sources do not say so and this is not inferred.

Debt events after the period: on 2026-10-20 the company issued notice to redeem all remaining 8.625% notes due 2030 (about 236 principal) at 100% plus accrued interest, expected on 2026-10-30 and funded from cash on hand; it expects to cut annualized cash interest by about 20 (Q3 10-Q page:16; Q3 release page:5). This is a subsequent event after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, announced and expected before the cutoff but not confirmed as completed in any source. The CP-1 handoff holds the leverage and liquidity figures before and after this event. Because the facility's early maturity trigger refers to more than 200 of the 2030 notes outstanding (Q3 10-Q page:11), completing the redemption would remove that trigger (Analyst Interpretation).

Dividends: a quarterly dividend of 0.275 per share was declared on 2026-10-15, payable 2026-12-03 to holders of record on 2026-11-06 (Q3 10-Q page:15). The record date is after the cutoff and is a future term.

fields.value: - The strongest reason for caution is that all debt terms and covenant levels rest on summaries in the notes, for example Q3 10-Q page:11: "a maximum total net leverage ratio of 3.50 to 1.00". A search of every source for covenant compliance statements, waivers and events of default found only risk-factor language and the "Defaults Upon Senior Securities. None." item in each quarterly report (for example Q3 10-Q page:38), and no ratio is reported against these levels. Mechanism: without the reported covenant ratio or the definitions, covenant headroom cannot be sourced, so CP-1 and CP-2 can only state the levels and say headroom is not supplied. This limits the covenant and liquidity conclusions, not the business or leverage description.

fields.value: The financial base is sound enough to support the downstream credit work, with a Medium confidence and named restrictions. On the filed balance sheet at 2026-09-30, total debt (current plus long-term, including finance leases, carrying value) was 1,480 against cash and cash equivalents of 1,161 and restricted cash of 37, giving net debt of 282. The company's trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA was 1,001, so total debt was 1.48x and net debt 0.28x on that definition. The debt stack is two senior note series (the 8.625% notes due 2030 and the 6.75% notes due 2033) plus finance leases, with a 1,000 secured revolving and letter of credit facility that has zero borrowings. Near-term maturities are small until the 2030 notes, which the company has called for redemption from cash on 2026-10-30; completion is announced, not evidenced. The base also carries four restrictions. First, adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation, restructuring, redomestication and other charges; on an unadjusted basis (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) the trailing figure is 867 and total debt is 1.71x, so the definition matters. Second, the credit agreement states a minimum interest coverage, a maximum total net leverage and a maximum secured net leverage, but the sources report no covenant ratio and do not define the covenant terms, so covenant headroom is Not supplied. Third, operating cash flow in the nine months to 2026-09-30 rose against the year-ago period only because of a working capital release; before working capital items it fell. Fourth, letters of credit, surety bonds, operating leases and a small supplier financing programme sit outside the debt total and are shown separately below. Revenue and segment profit are down year on year in 2026 on the effect of the Iran Conflict in the Middle East, North Africa and Asia region, while cost reductions held margins.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage. Evidence: total debt of 1,480 and company adjusted EBITDA for the trailing twelve months of 1,001 at 2026-09-30, against 1,485 and 1,067 at 2025-12-31. Risk mechanic: debt barely changed over nine months while trailing EBITDA fell, so gross leverage rose slightly even as net leverage fell on cash build. The decline in net leverage comes from cash, not from debt reduction, and cash includes trapped balances. Credit implication: leverage is moderate on any measure in the sources; it is sensitive to the EBITDA definition (1.48x on adjusted EBITDA, 1.71x on operating income plus depreciation and amortization), and the announced redemption would reduce gross debt without changing net debt materially because it uses cash.

fields.value: Coverage. Evidence: trailing cash interest paid of 111 at Q3 2026 against 125 for FY2025. Risk mechanic: cash interest paid is lumpy because the coupons are semiannual and the 2033 notes paid their first coupon on 2026-04-15; the trailing figure still contains payments on the larger 2030 notes before their 2025 partial redemption. Credit implication: coverage of cash interest is strong on adjusted EBITDA, and the run-rate burden should be lower after the redemption (the company expects annualized cash interest to fall by about 20, Q3 release page:5), but the ratio is not a covenant test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow quality. Evidence: operating cash flow of 503 against 408 in the nine months, but working capital items contributed 65 against (116). Risk mechanic: receivable collections released cash (186 against 22 a year earlier), which does not recur once balances normalise; the 10-Q attributes the increase to "increased cash from accounts receivable, partially offset by lower cash earnings and higher cash usage related to income taxes payable" (Q3 10-Q page:29). The Q3 tax provision of 4 includes a 56 valuation allowance release (Q3 10-Q page:14), so Q3 net income is not a clean earnings run-rate. Credit implication: free cash flow conversion is real but partly timing; adjusted free cash flow of 379 should be read with the working capital contribution.

fields.value: Liquidity. Evidence: cash of 1,161 and a revolving and letter of credit facility with zero borrowings. Risk mechanic: availability is reduced by letters of credit; the 10-K split means only the revolving portion can fund cash needs, while other letters of credit and surety bonds could be called. Credit implication: liquidity covers the 2030 notes call and the near term, and the minimum liquidity covenant is far below cash, but definitions are unseen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weatherford is a listed, widely held global oilfield services group that sells equipment and services across the well lifecycle through three segments: Drilling and Evaluation, Well Construction and Completions, and Production and Intervention. The consolidated reporting entity is Weatherford International plc, an Irish public limited company with principal executive offices in Houston, Texas. The sources disclose no sponsor, no controlling shareholder and no dividend recapitalisation history, so creditor control rests on the debt documents rather than on an owner. The creditor-relevant story in the sources is operating and structural. First, demand follows customer capital spending and rig activity, and in 2026 the Iran Conflict has cut regional activity even as oil prices were higher; revenue has fallen while margins were held by cost action. Second, receivable and cash concentration (a Mexican customer with late payments, Russian operations holding cash, cash that cannot be repatriated freely) can slow conversion of earnings to usable liquidity. Third, the capital structure was reshaped in the last twelve months: a 2025 refinancing into 6.75% notes due 2033, an equity-funded acquisition of NCS Multistage Holdings, Inc. that closed on 2026-09-01, an announced redemption of the remaining 8.625% notes due 2030 from cash, and a pending redomestication of the parent from Ireland to Delaware that shareholders approved on 2026-09-03 and that awaits court sanction. The terms of the redomestication that bear on lenders (guarantors, collateral, the intellectual property transition) are not described in the sources. Governance evidence is limited to documented actions: refinancing and redemption that reduce interest cost, continued dividends and buybacks funded from operating cash flow, and co-issuer additions on the notes whose purpose is not explained. This supports a Supportive to Neutral reading of issuer-level behaviour, with Insufficient Information on legal capacity. The view carries Medium confidence because filings control the facts, but the executed credit agreement, the indentures and the proxy statement that would show ownership are not in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues: the sources show one new bond issue in the last two years and none in 2026. On 2025-10-06 Weatherford International Ltd. issued 6.75% senior notes due 2033-10-15 (principal 1.2 billion as printed); the tender offer and redemption of most of the 8.625% senior notes due 2030 used the proceeds of that issue and cash on hand, and the company recorded a 39 loss on extinguishment and redemption premium (10-K page:84 and page:44; Documentary Fact). The mechanism for a creditor is lower coupon and a maturity pushed from 2030 to 2033 on most of the bond debt, with the stub of the 2030 notes (principal about 236) left outstanding until the October 2026 call. On 2025-09-18 the credit agreement was amended to raise the commitment from 720 to 1 billion with an accordion to 1.15 billion and to extend its maturity (10-K page:55; Documentary Fact); the amendment text is not supplied. No new borrowing is reported in the nine months to 2026-09-30 (CP-1 cash flow table; Q3 10-Q page:3 and page:4).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition: on 2026-05-31 Weatherford signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire NCS Multistage Holdings, Inc. for shares or a mix of shares and cash, subject to proration (Q2 10-Q page:14), and it closed on 2026-09-01 for total consideration of 128, made up of 13 cash net of cash acquired, 1.0 million ordinary shares valued at 101 and 7 for assumed equity awards (Q3 10-Q page:15; Documentary Fact). The acquired business brought tangible assets of 150, intangible assets and goodwill of 46 and liabilities of 34, plus 34 of noncontrolling interest (page:15). Management states that it expects "at least $15 million of cost synergies upon closing and integration" (Q2 release page:2; Management Language, not adopted). Mechanism: because most consideration was shares and assumed awards, the deal added little cash outflow or debt, so leverage effects are limited, but the 10-Q does not say whether NCS carried debt, and integration risk and cost remain. Appetite for further acquisitions is not inferred from one deal. The Q3 10-Q records that Advent-NCS Acquisition Limited Partnership, NCS's largest shareholder, received 357,159 shares, resold under a registered prospectus supplement (page:38); this is not a control position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Redomestication: the first proposal (Ireland to Texas, announced 2026-04-02) received over 60% support but not the 75% needed and failed in June 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:12; Q2 release page:5). An updated proposal to redomesticate to Delaware was approved by shareholders on 2026-09-03 and is subject to sanction by the High Court of Ireland and other steps, with completion expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:16). Management expects annual cash savings of 20 to 30 from 2027 (Q3 release page:6; Management Language). Related restructuring activities, including the planned intellectual property transition, are "being evaluated for their potential accounting and tax implications" (Q3 10-Q page:16). Creditor mechanism: a change of parent and a transfer of intellectual property can alter which entities hold assets, who guarantees the debt and how the collateral is arranged, and whether credit agreement or indenture conditions apply. The sources do not describe any of those effects, so the lender impact is Insufficient Information and the pending status must be carried into every consumer. The 2026-09-25 supplemental indenture adding Weatherford International Holding LLC as co-issuer of the 2033 notes and releasing its guarantee (Q3 10-Q page:10 and page:39) may be a step in this reorganisation, but the sources do not say so and this is not inferred.

This is a subsequent event after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, announced and expected before the cutoff but not confirmed as completed in any source. The CP-1 handoff holds the leverage and liquidity figures before and after this event. fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: revenue for nine months 2026 fell from 3,629 to 3,400 while rig counts and oil prices were higher (Q3 10-Q pages:2, 18, 19). Risk mechanic: the Iran Conflict removed regional activity in Middle East, North Africa and Asia, the group's largest region (10-K page:81; Q3 10-Q page:20), so revenue is driven by a regional shock and not by commodity prices alone; management expects recovery to be gradual and uncertain (Q3 10-Q page:29, Management Language). Credit implication: coverage and leverage metrics in CP-1 are exposed to a further or longer disruption; the timing of recovery is the key uncertainty. Counter-evidence: three segments and about 75 countries diversify the base, and sequential Q3 2026 revenue rose in North America and Latin America (Q3 release page:7, Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: cost of products and services was 69% of revenue in FY2025 against 65% as fixed costs fell more slowly than revenue (10-K page:42); nine-month operating income fell from 557 to 383 (Q3 10-Q page:2). Risk mechanic: fixed cost leverage cuts margins when volume falls; cost action (restructuring of 28) offsets only partly. Credit implication: free cash flow conversion shown in CP-1 depends on working capital release and cost savings that may not repeat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: the largest Mexican customer was 24% of receivables at 2025-12-31 and 14% at 2026-09-30 with a late payment history (10-K page:21; Q3 10-Q page:32); Russian operations held cash of 128 and 164 of cash cannot be immediately repatriated (Q3 10-Q pages:19, 31). Risk mechanic: slow collection raises working capital and factoring need; sanctions and exchange controls trap cash. Credit implication: usable liquidity is lower than headline cash; monitor receivable days and trapped cash. No logged conflict counters this translation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Sponsor alignment and structure. Evidence: no sponsor, no disclosed controlling holder, shareholder payouts covered by free cash flow, co-issuer changes unexplained, redomestication pending (see the governance table). Risk mechanic: creditor protection rests on documents not supplied and on management decisions about obligors and collateral during the corporate move. Credit implication: monitor the closing steps, any guarantor or collateral change and the indenture covenant limits on payouts before relying on structure. The dated sequence conflict on the redomestication counters any reading of a fixed plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Key uncertainties. Middle East recovery timing; redomestication terms and completion; completion of the October 2026 redemption; NCS integration and any acquired debt; covenant headroom (not reported). Credit implication: Medium confidence overall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weatherford International plc has a sound fundamental credit profile at the 2026-09-30 balance sheet date, with low reported leverage and ample liquidity, but its earnings are cyclical and currently depressed by Middle East disruption. The strongest support is total debt of USD 1,480 million, or 1.48x trailing company-defined adjusted EBITDA, against cash of USD 1,161 million and undrawn bank commitments of USD 766 million. The weakest point is the earnings and cash flow trend: nine-month 2026 revenue fell to USD 3,400 million and operating cash flow before working capital fell to USD 438 million. What decides the outcome is how fast regional activity recovers, and whether the pending redomestication or shareholder payouts change obligor and covenant protections that the sources do not reveal. Confidence is Medium. [CP-1 financial base view; CP-1A business and transaction view]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first finding a committee must read is that Weatherford carries little leverage on every measure the sources allow. Total debt of USD 1,480 million is 1.48x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,001 million and 1.71x EBITDA before add-backs of USD 867 million; net debt of USD 282 million is 0.28x. The ratio on the company's definition has crept up from 1.39x at 2025-12-31 because trailing EBITDA fell while debt was flat, and net leverage fell only because cash rose. [CP-1 leverage chart data and calculations 5 and 6]. The mechanism is that low leverage gives room to absorb a further earnings decline, but the cushion is in cash that is partly trapped, not in falling debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second finding is that liquidity is strong and the near-term maturity is already funded. Cash of USD 1,161 million is 4.40x the current portion of long-term debt of USD 264 million, which is mostly the 2030 notes that Weatherford called on 2026-10-20 for redemption from cash on 2026-10-30. Undrawn commitments are USD 766 million after letters of credit, of which only about USD 599 million can be borrowed for cash on the facility split disclosed in the annual report. Liquidity is 1.30x total debt, or 1.19x on the cash-drawable basis. Redemption completion is not evidenced, and the pro forma net debt after it would be about the same, since the notes are repaid with cash. [CP-1 liquidity, calculations 8 and 11; CP-1A transaction summary]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third finding is that earnings are weakening in 2026 and cash flow quality is lower than it looks. Nine-month 2026 revenue of USD 3,400 million is 6.3% below USD 3,629 million a year earlier and operating income of USD 383 million is 31.2% below USD 557 million, because the Iran Conflict cut Middle East, North Africa and Asia revenue even though oil prices and rig counts were higher. Operating cash flow rose to USD 503 million from USD 408 million only through a working capital release of USD 65 million against an outflow of USD 116 million, so cash flow before working capital fell by USD 86 million. The mechanism is operating leverage on a fixed cost base plus receivable timing, and it matters because free cash flow supports both debt service and shareholder payouts. [CP-1 cash flow tables and calculation 10; CP-1A operating model rows on the Iran Conflict and cost structure]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth finding is that concentrated receivables, trapped cash and contingent instruments can reduce usable liquidity. The largest Mexican customer was 14% of net receivables at 2026-09-30 and has a history of late payment; about USD 164 million of cash cannot be immediately repatriated, with USD 128 million held in Russian operations; and letters of credit and surety bonds totalling USD 1,065 million sit outside debt and can be called on breach of contract or performance. That total is 0.72x total debt and is not additive to the liquidity measure. [CP-1 claims outside the debt total; CP-1A concentration rows]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth finding is that the capital structure and legal perimeter are in transition and the sources do not describe the lender effects. Debt was refinanced into 6.75% notes due 2033 in 2025, NCS Multistage was acquired mostly for shares, and entities were added as co-issuers of the notes, most recently on 2026-09-25. The parent has shareholder approval to move from Ireland to a Delaware corporation, subject to court sanction, with a planned intellectual property transition under evaluation. The mechanism is that obligor, guarantor and collateral arrangements could change while the documents that govern them are not available. [CP-1A transaction summary, governance table and conflicts table]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Low reported leverage (Documentary Fact): total debt is 1.48x and net debt 0.28x of trailing company-defined adjusted EBITDA, and the interest burden is light, with adjusted EBITDA 9.02x trailing cash interest paid [CP-1]. Large liquidity (Documentary Fact): USD 1,161 million of cash and USD 766 million of undrawn commitments, with zero borrowings on the facility [CP-1]. A refinanced, longer debt profile (Documentary Fact): most bond debt now matures in 2033 and the remaining 2030 notes are called, which the company expects to reduce annualized cash interest by about USD 20 million (Management Language) [CP-1; CP-1A timeline]. Diversified operations (Documentary Fact): three well-lifecycle segments across about 75 countries, with most revenue earned internationally [CP-1A operating model]. Free cash flow covers payouts (Analyst Interpretation): nine-month 2026 adjusted free cash flow of USD 379 million exceeded the shareholder return of USD 113 million, which is 29.8% of it, and no debt-funded distribution is evidenced [CP-1; CP-1A ownership and capital allocation]. No sponsor or extraction behaviour is documented (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A governance table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Earnings are cyclical and falling in 2026 (Documentary Fact): revenue and operating income are lower and adjusted EBITDA for nine months fell 8.5% to USD 710 million from USD 776 million [CP-1]. Cash flow before working capital fell (Analyst Interpretation): the rise in reported operating cash flow depends on receivable collections that may not repeat [CP-1]. Regional and customer concentration (Documentary Fact): the largest region is the disrupted one, a Mexican customer has a late payment history, and Russia carries sanctions and cash access risk [CP-1A]. Fixed cost leverage (Documentary Fact): cost of products and services rose to 69% of revenue from 65% in FY2025 as costs fell more slowly than revenue [CP-1A]. Definition and covenant opacity (Insufficient Information): adjusted EBITDA is company-defined and covenant ratios and definitions are not reported, so headroom cannot be measured [CP-1]. Structural transition (Insufficient Information): the effect of the redomestication and the intellectual property transition on guarantors and collateral is undescribed, and ownership beyond a widely held listing is undisclosed [CP-1A].

fields.value: The gaps ledger above lists the ten evidence gaps with follow-up sources. In summary, the evidence limits that change a conclusion are the missing executed debt documents and covenant compliance figures (covenant headroom and structural statements stay restricted), the undescribed lender effects of the pending redomestication, the unconfirmed completion of the October 2026 redemption, and the cash-drawable portion of the facility. Limits that do not change a conclusion are text-only extraction, undisclosed backlog and pricing, and absent market data for relative value.
